title: Looking at a face is on the CDC list for two months
summary: Most babies look at a face by two months, the CDC says.
body: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention puts 'looks at your face' on the social milestones for two months. A milestone, on that page, is something most children, 75 percent or more, do by the stated age. The Learn the Signs materials are not a substitute for a standardized, validated developmental screening tool. Other countries publish other lists, so this line is the American checklist, not a verdict on one baby.

sources.title: Milestones by 2 Months
sources.author: CDC
sources.note: Supports 'Looks at your face' as a milestone most children (75% or more) do by two months, and the screening-tool disclaimer.
